fields.documentation:
Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a **Material** tag with the values **Solid** and **Stone**, And another single tag **Ore**.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with **Material** and **Ore** the end result would be the following list of tags: **Ore**, **Material**, **Solid**, **Stone**, **Material=Solid** and **Material=Stone**.
Ignored - the station id comes from the asset filename, not this key. Kept as a schema field for editor display only.
Display name/description localization keys plus the icon item id, shown at the station's engage prompt and any station-listing UI.
The localization key resolved client-side for the station's display name; null = no name shown.
The localization key resolved client-side for the station's description; null = no description shown.
An item id whose icon represents this station in any station-listing UI (the ability-icon convention).
The work-loop cadence, duration/exit bounds, per-cycle contributions, looping flag, and optional idle-practice mode.
Milliseconds per work cycle (one Convert transaction / one implicit-program run). Reader-defaults to 5000.
The hard session-duration cap in milliseconds; the heartbeat stops the session once elapsed. Reader-defaults to 600000 (10 minutes).
The walk-off EXIT trigger radius in meters from the engage position (not an anti-idle guard). Reader-defaults to 1.5.
Whether the station block is exclusive to one worker at a time (a second player's engage is denied while occupied). Reader-defaults to true.

Amounts posted on every completed cycle, forwarded verbatim on the cycle-completed event; the engine never interprets a channel itself. SCALED: each Amount is multiplied by the resolved tool multiplier (Tool.PowerScale) and, on an idle cycle, pre-scaled by Work.Idle.Fraction. Contrast Roll.Grants.Contributions, which is one-shot and never scaled.

The namespaced channel id this contribution posts to (e.g. 'yourmod:crop_quality'), opaque to this engine - it is never resolved here, only forwarded. Pick it from the rpgstations:channels dropdown, or declare your own via ContributionChannelRegistry.
Optional channel-interpreted argument, opaque to this engine - whatever the channel's owner documents (commonly the specific thing being credited).
The amount posted. Scaling is decided by WHERE this entry is authored - see the owning group's documentation.
Opt-in no-material idle practice mode; null/absent Enabled = off (a NO_INPUTS start is denied).
Opts into no-material idle practice when no conversion is runnable. Default false (a NO_INPUTS start denies).
Milliseconds per idle cycle. Reader-defaults to 3x the effective Work.CycleMs, floored at 2x it.
The fraction of a normal cycle's Work.PerCycleContributions amounts an idle cycle posts (tool multiplier forced to 1.0, no conversion/loot). Reader-defaults to 0.1, clamped to [0,1].
Does the program (implicit or authored Steps) re-run every CycleMs? Default true (the classic loop); false completes the whole session after one run (the ritual shape).
The Convert recipe: authored Conversions and/or a FromCrafting derivation from native recipes.
Hand-authored input-to-output conversions, evaluated FIRST (before any FromCrafting-derived ones).
The conversion inputs (native CraftingRecipe.Input shape): each an Ingredient, exactly one of ItemId | ResourceTypeId. Every entry must be available for the cycle to run.
The conversion outputs (native CraftingRecipe.Output shape): each an exact-ItemId Ingredient. Every entry needs inventory room for the cycle to run.
Optional per-conversion pace override in ms; highest precedence (> NativeTime > Work.CycleMs). Null = none.
Optional source-category tag the multi-output picker groups by; the deriver stamps it from the matched native recipe category (else bench id). Null = untagged.
Derive additional Conversions from the engine's own native crafting/processing recipes; null = no derivation.
Native recipe categories to derive Conversions from (e.g. 'WoodPlanks'); a pack-added category in the set just works.
Native BenchRequirement bench ids this station's recipes scope to (id-ref-only string match).
The recipe kinds to derive: 'Crafting' and/or 'Processing'; absent = both.
Linear transform (Scale*TimeSeconds + OffsetMs) over each derived recipe's native time; defaults stay slower than vanilla.
Multiplier (m) on the recipe's native time; reader-defaults to 1.0 (stretch, never speed up below vanilla).
Additive floor (b) in milliseconds added after scaling; reader-defaults to 2000 so a station is never instant like vanilla.
Per-cycle output-quantity transform applied to whichever conversion runs (authored or derived); null = each conversion's own authored quantity, unchanged.
Flat output quantity per conversion BEFORE Scale/Bonus; null = use each conversion's own authored output quantity.
Multiplier on the base quantity, rounded to the nearest whole item; reader-defaults to 1.0 (no scaling).
Optional factor-driven bonus ladder adding extra output (e.g. a better tool yields more); null = no bonus.
Weighted factor references summed into the ladder value (e.g. tool power plus tool quality); empty = a constant 0.
Thresholds over the summed value; the HIGHEST floor whose Min is reached contributes its Add. Empty = no bonus.
The summed factor value at or above which this floor applies; reader-defaults to 0.
Extra items added when this floor is the reached one; may be fractional (2.5 = two always plus a 50% chance of a third). Reader-defaults to 0.
Lower clamp on the final quantity; null = the engine's own 1-item floor.
Upper clamp on the final quantity; null = uncapped.
The movement lock while working: the default self-effect hold, or the Mount knob family (seated/standing mount).
Whether the movement-lock effect applies while working. Reader-defaults to true. Ignored while a Block-surface Mount is active (the mount itself is the lock).
The native EntityEffect asset id re-applied every heartbeat under decay-as-release. Reader-defaults to 'RPG_Station_Hold'. A bare id, never a timed EffectRef - the hold's lifetime is engine-owned.
Whether taking damage stops the session. Reader-defaults to true.
The alternate mount-based hold strategy (Block seat or Entity standing mount); null = the default self-effect hold above.
The mount mechanism union discriminator: 'Block' (native seat mount, default) or 'Entity' (standing work mount). Unrecognized values fall to Block with a validator warn.
The standing work mount's sub-knobs; read only when Surface is 'Entity' (a validator warns if authored under 'Block').
The mount attachment offset from the anchor entity, in blocks (X right, Y up, Z forward).
The X component; unauthored means 0 (each axis is independently optional).
The Y component; unauthored means 0 (each axis is independently optional).
The Z component; unauthored means 0 (each axis is independently optional).
Whether a heartbeat walk-off check dismounts the player (no native auto-dismount for this route). Reader-defaults to true; false = hard-lock until crouch/re-press.
Whether the anchor may be WASD-steered by the mounted player. Reader-defaults to false (a per-heartbeat snap-back defeats native steering); true is validator-flagged as untested.
Diagnostic/authoring aid: an item id the invisible anchor renders as a dropped-item-style prop, so its position is visible in-game. Null = no visual (the shipped default).
The held-tool gate (tag/gather/id match routes), tool-power contribution scaling, durability drain, and minimum-durability start gate.
Native tag family match (e.g. {"Family":["Dagger"]}): matches ANY-of the values per key against the held Item's raw tags.
The functional gather-power match route: a native GatherType plus a minimum power floor.
The native GatherType id the held tool's ItemToolSpec must report.
The minimum ItemToolSpec power the held tool must report for this GatherType.
The FALLBACK exact/underscore-segment item id match route, for modded tools with no matching tag or gather spec.

Maps held-tool power to the multiplier applied to every Work.PerCycleContributions amount on a real cycle (forwarded as the cycle event's toolMultiplier); forced 1.0 on an idle cycle. Null = the multiplier stays neutral 1.0 regardless of held tool.
The native GatherType id whose power is read off the held tool each cycle for this scale.
The tool power treated as the neutral 1.0x baseline the held tool's power is divided by.
The power curve exponent applied to (heldPower / ReferencePower). Reader-defaults to 1.0 (linear).
The floor the resolved multiplier clamps to. Reader-defaults to 0.5.
The ceiling the resolved multiplier clamps to. Reader-defaults to 2.0.
Opt-in held-tool durability drain per swing and/or per cycle; null = no drain.
Durability points drained from the held tool per swing cue. Reader-defaults to 0 (off).
Durability points drained from the held tool per completed cycle. Reader-defaults to 0 (off).
Minimum held-tool durability (0-100) required to START working; null = no wear gate. Checked at engage only, so a session already running is never cut short by wear.
Conditional loot for the implicit action: a LootRef (referenced Lootables + inline Rolls).
The third-person camera pull while working, plus the optional fixed-look FaceBlock preset.
The camera route: 'ThirdPerson' (default, the pull applies) or 'None' (no camera pull at all - a mounted station with no authored Camera also defaults to none).
Whether the third-person camera is locked in place while working (blocks player-driven camera rotation). Reader-defaults to true.
Whether the fixed-look FaceBlock camera preset applies (mouse-driven spin is fully frozen, not just locked). Only takes effect when the camera is applied at all.
The StationCameraPreset recipe id the FaceBlock route applies (the exact ServerCameraSettings field combination); null = the engine's default FROZEN recipe.
The work emote id plus the optional per-swing cadence/impact cue layer.
The registered EmoteAsset id looped while working; null = no work animation played.
The optional per-swing cadence layer (re-fires a one-shot cue on an interval); null = no swing layer.
Milliseconds between swing cues while working; a non-looping EmoteId needs this authored or the work animation never re-fires.
The presentation cue fired together with each swing re-fire; null = the swing plays with no extra sound/particles.
An optional delayed impact cue scheduled off this swing; null = no impact cue.
Milliseconds after the swing before the impact cue fires. Null/non-positive = fire together with the swing.
The presentation cue fired at the scheduled impact moment.
The Action-slot clip id for a SEAT-MODE swing (plays against the held item's own ItemPlayerAnimations set). Null/blank falls to the 'Chop' default.
The CYCLE-complete presentation moment: sound/particles/animation cues fired at the block each finished cycle.
The SESSION-COMPLETION presentation moment, played on a non-silent stop with at least one completed cycle. Null = silent completion.
The start gate: an optional permission node plus factor Conditions, evaluated once at engage.
Session-scoped placed-input custody; null = the classic direct-inventory Consume/Produce flow.
The puppet presentation route: mount the player, hide their body, spawn a skinned visual performing the work. Null = the classic in-body worker.
Named cosmetic flair overrides, keyed by flair id; each entry overlays its non-null Moments onto the base presentation when that flair is unlocked for the player.
An open moment id (cycle/swing/impact/rare_find/completion, or step:<actionId>:<stepId>) to a Presentation overlay; each authored leaf overlays the base moment's own leaves, per moment id.
Named, authored-order multi-action overrides; null/empty means the single implicit 'work' action built from this station's own groups.
The multi-output picker knob group (decision 50); default = locked categories shown greyed.
Whether tool-gated (locked) output categories render greyed in the picker (default true); false hides them entirely.

Tags are a general way to describe an asset that can be interpreted by other systems in a way they see fit.

For example you could tag something with a **Material** tag with the values **Solid** and **Stone**, And another single tag **Ore**.

Tags will be expanded into a single list of tags automatically. Using the above example with **Material** and **Ore** the end result would be the following list of tags: **Ore**, **Material**, **Solid**, **Stone**, **Material=Solid** and **Material=Stone**.
